name: Zo Computer

modes.label: Zo Basic subscription, one always-on computer (4 cores / 32 GB) - $18/mo
modes.commit_note: Monthly subscription per workspace; prorated on plan change
modes.note: Flat $18/month per workspace (hour = fee/730). Includes $10/mo AI credits (not compute), 5 hosted services, 3 custom domains. Personal-server product, not a sandbox API: one computer per workspace.

modes.label: Zo Pro subscription, one always-on computer (16 cores / 128 GB) - $64/mo
modes.commit_note: Monthly subscription per workspace; prorated on plan change
modes.note: Flat $64/month per workspace (hour = fee/730). Includes $40/mo AI credits (not compute), 10 hosted services, 5 custom domains. Personal-server product, not a sandbox API: one computer per workspace.

modes.label: Zo Ultra subscription, one always-on computer (64 cores / 512 GB) - $200/mo
modes.commit_note: Monthly subscription per workspace; prorated on plan change
modes.note: Flat $200/month per workspace (hour = fee/730). Includes $100/mo AI credits (not compute), 50 hosted services, 10 custom domains. Personal-server product, not a sandbox API: one computer per workspace.

modes.label: N Basic workspaces sized to peak concurrency (part-time use)
modes.commit_note: Monthly subscription per workspace; prorated on plan change
modes.note: Each parallel sandbox = one Zo workspace on Basic ($18/mo, 4 cores/32 GB, always-on). Valid only if a session fits one computer and workspaces are reused across sessions; running many workspaces as a fleet is not a documented use (ToS/account limits unverified).

plans.name: Paid workspace subscription (fee priced in modes)
plans.note: The Basic/Pro/Ultra fees ($18/$64/$200) ARE the compute and are carried in the modes (always_on_month_per_instance / pool month) to avoid double counting. Included AI credits $10/$40/$100 are for AI usage only.

plans.name: Free Trial (14 days)
plans.note: 14-day computer + AI trial, limited CPU/memory, sleeps when idle, then recovery-only. Not a lasting plan.

plans.name: Teams (company Zo on Ultra + teammate Basic logins)
plans.note: Shared company computer on Ultra ($200/mo) plus each teammate's own Basic plan ($18/person/month) as the seat; team of 5 = $272/mo. Onboarding is manual (leave email, Zo connects accounts, usually same day). Each teammate's Basic also carries its own 4-core/32 GB computer.

features.ip_note: Built-in Chromium browser tools (open/view/use webpage) on the Zo server, plus optional control of the user's local Chrome via the desktop app; no proxy/stealth/CAPTCHA options documented.

caveats: Personal cloud computer + AI agent, not a sandbox API: one always-on server per workspace; all modes flagged 'alt'. Fleet = N separate workspace subscriptions (not a documented use).
Flat monthly subscription: no per-hour billing, so part-time use pays the full $18/$64/$200.
Plan compute is large for the price (Basic 4 cores/32 GB) but whether cores/RAM are dedicated or caps on shared Modal/Daytona hardware is not stated.
Included AI credits ($10/$40/$100) cover AI usage only, not compute; not modeled as included_usd.
Isolation not stated; compute providers are Modal and Daytona (security page) -> modeled as container.
Zo restarts periodically for updates/snapshots even on paid plans; only registered services come back automatically.
Storage beyond 100 GB ('100GB+') unpriced; egress, IPv4, regions, compliance undocumented.
Free Trial: 14 days, limited resources, sleeps when idle, then recovery-only (not usable as a free tier).

Teams pricing is now published (was 'no prices' in the regime file): Ultra $200/mo for the shared company computer + $18/person/month (each teammate's own Basic) = per-seat cost. 'No contracts, no per-user platform fees'.
Multiple workspace subscriptions on one billing account are possible (docs mention it), which weakly supports the fleet-basic mode, but paid media is then blocked.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: Snapshots of the user's filesystem occur regularly to ensure past data can always be recovered.
snapshot_auto.note: Only periodic filesystem backup snapshots (Zo 'restarts periodically to pick up updates and snapshots', services.md), not snapshot-on-stop/idle; paid computers are always-on. No memory state. Recovery appears to be via support/recovery sessions, not a user restore.

own_agent_api.quote: Send a message to your Zo and get a response. This is the same Zo you talk to in the app — your files, integrations, and tools are all available.
own_agent_api.note: POST https://api.zo.computer/zo/ask drives Zo's own built-in agent: prompt, SSE streaming (stream:true), follow-ups via conversation_id, model_name/persona_id override, JSON-schema structured output. No list/resume-conversations endpoint. Claude Code and Codex subscriptions can be used as the model provider (Settings > AI Providers), but the API drives the Zo agent, not the claude/codex CLIs directly. Also an MCP server exposing Zo's tools.

harness_api.quote: Send a message to your Zo and get a response. This is the same Zo you talk to in the app — your files, integrations, and tools are all available.
harness_api.note: POST https://api.zo.computer/zo/ask drives Zo's own built-in agent: prompt, SSE streaming (stream:true), follow-ups via conversation_id, model_name/persona_id override, JSON-schema structured output. No list/resume-conversations endpoint. Claude Code and Codex subscriptions can be used as the model provider (Settings > AI Providers), but the API drives the Zo agent, not the claude/codex CLIs directly. Also an MCP server exposing Zo's tools.

ingress_rules.quote: You can also set an HTTP service to **private**, in which case it lives at `*.zo.computer` and requires you to sign in.
ingress_rules.note: Per-service choice: http public (*.zocomputer.io, no auth) or private (sign-in required); sites private by default; 'process' mode has no endpoint; you choose which local port each service exposes. But 'TCP services are always public, with no auth in front of them'. No IP allowlists. Plus temporary public TCP tunnels (proxy_local_service tool).

isolation.quote: Modal provides cloud compute. ... Daytona provides cloud compute.
isolation.note: derived: Zo does not state its own isolation tech; the underlying compute providers it names (Modal, Daytona) run workloads as container-based sandboxes, so isolation is modeled as container (shared-kernel), not a dedicated VM/microVM.

image_oci.quote: Own a real home on the internet with your own personal cloud.
image_oci.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Zo provisions one preconfigured Linux computer per workspace; there is no documented way to start it from a custom Docker/OCI image.

nested_virt.quote: Modal provides cloud compute. ... Daytona provides cloud compute.
nested_virt.note: derived: not documented; underlying container-based sandbox providers (Modal, Daytona) do not expose /dev/kvm to guest workloads, so nested virtualization is not available.

desktop.quote: Zo has a real Chromium browser running on your computer.
desktop.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Zo exposes a managed Chromium browser and a terminal/file interface, but no VNC/RDP graphical desktop of the cloud computer itself; the 'Zo desktop app' is a local client on the user's own machine, not a remote GUI.

anti_bot.quote: Zo has a real Chromium browser running on your computer. You sign into sites in that browser once, and from then on Zo can act on those sites as you.
anti_bot.note: No stealth/fingerprint-evasion features documented for the built-in browser; relies on the user's own signed-in session rather than anti-bot bypass tooling.

captcha_solving.quote: To protect account signup and login from automated abuse, we use Cloudflare Turnstile, a bot-detection service provided by Cloudflare, Inc.
captcha_solving.note: No CAPTCHA-solving feature is offered to users; Zo itself uses CAPTCHA-style bot detection (Turnstile) to block automated signups, the opposite capability.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Snapshots of the user's filesystem occur regularly to ensure past data can always be recovered.
snapshot_on_demand.note: Only automatic, periodic filesystem backup snapshots are documented; there is no API/CLI to trigger a snapshot/checkpoint on demand.

volume_attach.quote: All plans include 100 GB of cloud storage, access to the Zo MCP Server, and bringing your own API keys.
volume_attach.note: Storage is a single included disk per workspace (100 GB, 'Storage beyond 100GB+' unpriced); no documented feature to attach separate extra volumes.

volume_shared.quote: Own a real home on the internet with your own personal cloud.
volume_shared.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. One always-on computer per workspace with no multi-machine volume feature; there is no way to mount one volume across several running machines.

live_resize.quote: Monthly subscription per workspace; prorated on plan change
live_resize.note: CPU/RAM only changes by switching subscription tier (Basic/Pro/Ultra); no documented ability to resize a running machine's CPU/RAM live without recreating/restarting it.

lang_python.quote: A custom backend in Node, Python, Go, Ruby, Rust, or anything else that runs on Linux
lang_python.note: Full Linux sandbox with root access; Python runs out of the box (also used as an example entrypoint: `python3 app.py`).

lang_node.quote: A custom backend in Node, Python, Go, Ruby, Rust, or anything else that runs on Linux
lang_node.note: Node.js is explicitly listed; Sites are also built on Bun/Hono (a Node-compatible JS runtime).

egress_allowlist.quote: Access the internet and download files and programs
egress_allowlist.note: No documented provider-side outbound allow/deny list, no-internet mode, or egress security-group rules; the computer has open internet access by default.

egress_http_rules.quote: Access the internet and download files and programs
egress_http_rules.note: No HTTP method/path-level egress rule feature is documented anywhere in the guides or security page.

secret_proxy.note: Users bring their own API keys, stored/used by Zo (e.g. Settings > AI Providers, connected integrations); no documented first-party HTTP-credential-injection proxy that keeps secrets out of the machine entirely.

static_egress_ip.quote: Own a real home on the internet with your own personal cloud.
static_egress_ip.note: No fixed/static outbound IP is offered or documented; public_ipv4 is also false in the card.

max_session_h.note: Paid plans are always-on (Basic/Pro/Ultra) with no documented maximum session length; the computer runs continuously until stopped/cancelled, aside from periodic restarts for updates/snapshots which are not a session-length cap.

pause_resume.quote: Paid plans keep your computer always-on, so services, sites, and automations stay reachable around the clock.
pause_resume.note: The 'computer' itself has no user-facing pause/resume: paid plans are always-on; the Free Trial computer sleeps when idle and, after 14 days, only offers one-time recovery sessions, not resume. The word 'pause/resume' in the API only applies to individual hosted services/automation tasks (registered service on/off, task pause flag), not the machine.

fork.quote: Monthly paid plans add always-on compute, higher limits, included monthly AI credits, and connections for coding agents like Claude Code, Codex, and Gemini.
fork.note: No mention anywhere in the docs (guides, API reference, billing, security) of duplicating/cloning a workspace or computer into a new one; each plan is one persistent workspace/computer. Searched for 'duplicate', 'clone', 'fork' across the full docs export — no such feature.

fork_running.note: No fork feature at all (see fork claim), so cloning a running machine without stopping it is a fortiori unsupported.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: Snapshots of the user's filesystem occur regularly to ensure past data can always be recovered.
memory_snapshot_fork.note: Only periodic filesystem-only backup snapshots for recovery, not process-memory snapshots and not a fork/clone primitive; no memory-state cloning is documented anywhere.

computer_use.quote: The public surface is small: one endpoint to talk to your Zo, plus discovery endpoints for models and personas. Send a message to your Zo and get a response.
computer_use.note: Zo's own internal agent can screenshot/click inside its built-in browser ('Ask Zo to take a screenshot and tell you what it sees. From there you can tell it where to click.'), but there is no first-party API for an external caller/developer to drive a desktop or browser directly by screenshot+click coordinates -- the only public API is POST /zo/ask (natural-language prompt to Zo's own agent). No desktop-level computer-use API exists at all.

custom_image.quote: All files are stored using non-proprietary file formats in a portable, open-source container image format. The user's filesystem data can be provided in container image format if requested.
custom_image.note: Container image format is used for export/backup of the user's filesystem, not as a way to boot a workspace from a customer-supplied image. No docs describe starting a Zo computer from a custom Docker/OCI image; each plan provisions Zo's own fixed environment.

wake_on_request.quote: Hosted services include public websites and custom self-hosted services. They're not reachable while your computer is asleep.
wake_on_request.note: On the only plan where the computer sleeps (Free Trial), incoming requests to hosted services do NOT wake it -- they simply fail while asleep; the user must open the app to boot it. Paid plans never sleep, so there's nothing to wake automatically either way.

auto_stop_idle.quote: Paid plans keep your computer always-on, so services, sites, and automations stay reachable around the clock.
auto_stop_idle.note: The priced/modeled plans (Basic/Pro/Ultra) are explicitly always-on with no idle auto-stop. (Only the unpriced Free Trial computer sleeps when idle, and that plan isn't modeled as a billed mode.)

volumes.quote: All plans include 100 GB of cloud storage, access to the Zo MCP Server, and bringing your own API keys.
volumes.note: Storage is described only as a single flat included allotment (100 GB) per workspace; no docs mention attachable/extra persistent volumes, volume sizes, or per-GB pricing for additional volumes -- searched the full docs export for 'volume' with no hits.

public_ipv4.quote: Publishing a site creates an HTTP user service under the hood. The site runs a production build and gets a dedicated, memorable URL that works from anywhere.
public_ipv4.note: All inbound access is via HTTPS/TCP hostnames (*.zocomputer.io, custom domains) proxied by Cloudflare/Zo's routing layer; no mention of a dedicated/public IPv4 address anywhere in docs -- searched full docs export for 'ipv4'/'public ip'/'static ip' with no hits.

gpu.quote: Plans at a glance ... Compute: Always-on, 4 CPU / 32 GB RAM / 16 CPU / 128 GB RAM / 64 CPU / 512 GB RAM
gpu.note: All three paid tiers are described purely by CPU core count and RAM; the word 'GPU' does not appear anywhere in the full documentation export. Zo Computer is a personal cloud CPU workstation product (backed by Modal/Daytona containers), not a GPU cloud.

windows.quote: The Linux app ships as a Debian/Ubuntu .deb package.
windows.note: Windows/Mac downloads referenced in the docs are the desktop CLIENT app (file-sync UI) that connects to your cloud workspace; the workspace/computer itself runs as a Linux container on Modal/Daytona infrastructure (per security.md's 'container image format' and infra providers). No Windows machine option is offered.

macos.quote: Modal provides cloud compute. Daytona provides cloud compute.
macos.note: The cloud workspace runs on Modal/Daytona container infrastructure, i.e. Linux; macOS is only referenced for the desktop client app and for local iMessage integration ('macOS only'), never as a cloud machine OS option.

arm64.note: The only arm64 reference is the Linux desktop CLIENT .deb package architecture, not an arm64 option for the cloud workspace/computer itself; no docs describe choosing a CPU architecture for the workspace.

self_host.quote: Whenever possible, services are hosted on the user's personal server ... Our long-term vision is to enable running Zo on any machine.
self_host.note: Explicitly framed as a future 'long-term vision', not a current capability -- today Zo only runs as a hosted cloud workspace on Modal/Daytona; there is no documented way to self-host the Zo server/application today.

byoc.quote: Zo Computer currently uses the following infrastructure and service providers: Modal ... Daytona ... provides cloud compute.
byoc.note: Compute is provisioned on Zo's own Modal/Daytona accounts for all customers; no option is documented to deploy Zo into a customer-owned cloud account.

open_source.quote: All files are stored using non-proprietary file formats in a portable, open-source container image format ... we aim to store all AI memories and search indexes ... using open-weight embedding models and open-source software.
open_source.note: Only the file-storage FORMAT and some third-party components/models used internally are open; the Zo application/agent/server itself (the core product) has no published license or public source repo -- 'open-source' appearances in docs refer to file formats, bundled third-party tools (e.g. OpenCode), or the aspiration to use open components, not the product's own source code.

private_network.quote: You can also set an HTTP service to private, in which case it lives at *.zo.computer and requires you to sign in.
private_network.note: 'Private' only means sign-in-gated HTTPS at a public hostname (or private TCP tunnels are stated to be always public with no auth); there is no VPC/private-network/peering feature -- each workspace is an isolated single-tenant computer with no documented private networking between machines.

guest_firewall.quote: Modal provides cloud compute. ... Daytona provides cloud compute.
guest_firewall.note: derived: Zo's isolation is modeled as shared-kernel 'container' (not a full VM/microVM) backed by Modal/Daytona multi-tenant infrastructure. Multi-tenant container platforms of this kind typically do not grant guests CAP_NET_ADMIN or a usable iptables/nftables inside the sandbox network namespace, and no such capability is documented anywhere in Zo's guides or security page.

soc2.quote: This document explains the security characteristics of Zo Computer and helps users and organizations make an educated risk assessment.
soc2.note: Zo's dedicated security/trust page itemizes every infrastructure and service subprocessor in detail but never mentions a SOC 2 report, trust center, or attestation of its own; this is the kind of page that would link one if it existed. (One of Zo's own subprocessors, Daytona, has published its own SOC 2 Type II — but that is Daytona's certification, not Zo's.)

hipaa.quote: This document explains the security characteristics of Zo Computer and helps users and organizations make an educated risk assessment.
hipaa.note: No mention of HIPAA eligibility or a Business Associate Agreement anywhere in Zo's security page, guides, or pricing/Teams pages. Zo is a consumer/personal-cloud-computer product with no enterprise compliance program documented.

sso.quote: Set your team size on this page and leave your email; we follow up to collect your teammates' emails. Once the company Zo is on Ultra and each teammate is on Basic, we connect everyone, usually the same day.
sso.note: Team access is provisioned manually by Zo staff connecting individual personal accounts (each teammate keeps their own Basic-plan login), not via SAML/OIDC single sign-on with a corporate IdP. No SSO/SAML/OIDC feature is mentioned anywhere in Zo's docs.

eu_data_residency.quote: Own a real home on the internet with your own personal cloud.
eu_data_residency.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Zo has no region selector anywhere (card's `regions` field is null); one workspace/computer is simply provisioned on Zo's Modal/Daytona compute without any documented choice of geography, so EU-only data placement cannot be guaranteed or requested.

usage_api.quote: The Zo API lets you interact with your Zo from scripts, automations, or other apps. POST /zo/ask, GET /models/available, GET /personas/available.
usage_api.note: granularity: account-only; cost: no; Zo Computer is a flat monthly subscription product ($18/$64/$200/mo) with no public API for retrieving workspace usage or billing data. The API only exposes conversation, model listing, and persona management. Billing is account-only (one plan per workspace) with no per-machine usage tracking available.

locations_quote: Modal provides cloud compute. ... Daytona provides cloud compute.
